cycle_position.summary: SFR cap rates rose to 7.3% in Q4 2025 (+194 bps since 2021) as rents outpaced home prices — income yields improving. BTR development still elevated (~69,000 units started in the 12 months ending Sept 2025, 7.2% of all single-family starts) but Q1 2026 starts fell back on financing costs, multifamily supply competition, and congressional legislative risk aimed at institutional SFR ownership. Occupancy near long-run averages; rent growth moderated but steady.

supply_demand.note: Legislative risk (institutional-ownership bills in Congress) froze parts of the development market in early 2026 — a watch item that does NOT bind a natural-person buyer of scattered SFRs.

debt_terms.value: Same conventional investor stack as 2-4 unit multifamily (see multifamily.json); DSCR products widely offered on SFR.

small_investor_verdict.entry_vehicle: Scattered-site SFRs bought individually as a natural person; BTR communities are institutional-only (LP/REIT exposure if desired).
small_investor_verdict.reasoning: 7.3% average cap beats institutional multifamily by ~230 bps and the anti-institutional legislative mood is a tailwind for small buyers. But single-tenant vacancy risk (100% vacant or 100% full per house) and no small-landlord exemption leverage make it a complement to, not a substitute for, the 2-4 unit core strategy.
